However, the then learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) and the Judge of the commercial court No. 2 has passed the decree against all the defendant who has caused loss of the plaintiff in connivance with each other; as such the decretal amount with interest is to be realized from the defendants jointly and severally 

 7. Mr AF Hasan Ariff the learned advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellant-defendant Nos. 1 and 2, at the very outset of his argument has tried to bring our attention in the recital of the plaint which was filed for recovery of admitted loan amount to tune of Taka 16,40,000, granted to defendant No. 4 in the form of Over draft for the purpose of opening LC; as such when the money suit is found to have been filed for recovery of such loan with interest in terms of agreement the question of liability of other agency like agent does not, at all, arise and must be kept out of consideration. Mr Arif, the learned advocate, further submits that in no way this type of alleged facts of connivance of causing loss of the plaintiff can be brought within the mischief of money suit which has been filed for the purpose of recovery of admitted loan granted in favour of the defendant No. 4 who has allowed the court to pass an ex-parte decree against him. Moreover, the indemnity bond as alleged by the plaintiff was duly issued at the relevant period facilitating the importer defendant No. 4 to release the imported goods at an earliest opportunity because original documents was not available at the time of the arrival of the vessel on 8-7-1982; as such to avoid demurrage it was decided to release the goods in favour of the importer by taking indemnity bond, duly indorsed by the Bank where LC was opened. In support of his contention Mr Arif has referred a letter issued by the Janata Bank on 7-2-1983 addressed to Lieutenant SM Ahmad, Bangladesh Navy, Staff Offices to SZ ML A-9, Port Rest House, Chittagong but unfortunately he has not been examined during the course of trial. 

 8. On the other hand, Mr Masud Ahmed Sayeed the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent submits that in a money suit all the defendants are jointly and severally liable to pay the decretal amount; as such it is open to the decree holder to execute the decree against any of the defendant which decree holder may deem fit and proper. 

 9. Mr Sayeed further submits that since defendant No. 4 is admittedly a loanee to the tune of Taka 16,40,000 which was given in the form of Over-draft to open LC for importing Powder Milk and there can be no scope to deny the allegation brought against him since it has neither been paid nor any way it has been adjusted with the plaintiff-Bank. In support of sanction of such loan in favour of the defendant No. 4 the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant has referred a series of documents exhibits 1-11. Mr Sayeed has given much emphasis on the fact of the delivery of the goods on the basis of false documents like indemnity bond which was not, at all indorsed by the Bank; as such the court below has rightly made an observation that delivery of the imported goods in favour of the defendant No. 3 by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 was absolutely illegal for which they are to be held responsible and liable to pay compensation for it. The learned advocate further submits that the learned Judge of the court below though has decreed in the form of the compensation against the defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 3 but virtually the amount as has been decreed is a loan amount to be recovered from the defendant No.4 with interest. 

 17. In the light of the above observation we are to says that the decree as has been given by the court below will remain good and to be executed or implemented against defendant No,4 alone. Decree against defendants Nos. 1 & 2, carrier of goods, affording the plaintiff an opportunity to realize the amount in the form of compensation in the Money Suit filed for recovery of loan is hereby set-aside. 

 18. In the result, the appeal is allowed in part. The decree passed in favour of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 is hereby set-aside and decree passed against other defendants will remain good. Plaintiff is at liberty to realize the amount from the loanee the defendant No. 4 with cost as has been given by the court below.
